paragraphs.title: Moses Calls the People and Reminds Them of the Covenant

easy.question: Whom did Moses call at the beginning?
answers: All Israel
The king of Moab
The priests only
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Moses called all Israel.”

easy.question: Where did the Lord make the covenant with Israel?
answers: Jerusalem
Horeb
Egypt
easy.explanation: The verse says that the Lord made the covenant with Israel at Horeb.

easy.question: What were the Israelites required to do after learning the statutes and judgments?
answers: Go up the mountain
Tell them to the nations
Keep and do them
easy.explanation: Moses commanded them to learn, keep, and do the statutes and judgments.

medium.question: In the phrase “The Lord made a covenant with us,” what does “made” mean?
answers: Established or formed
Broke or canceled
Forgot or concealed
medium.explanation: In this context, “made” means established or formed a covenant.

medium.question: What order of actions is presented in verse 1?
answers: Do, learn, hear
Hear, learn, keep and do
Keep, hear, learn
medium.explanation: First Israel hears the words, then learns them, and finally keeps and does them.

medium.question: Why did Moses stand between the Lord and Israel at that time?
answers: Because Israel was afraid of the fire
Because Moses did not hear the Lord
Because the people were not near the mountain
medium.explanation: The people were afraid of the fire, so Moses served as an intermediary.

challenge.question: What is emphasized by Moses saying that the covenant was made “with us,” not only with their fathers?
answers: The covenant belonged only to the wilderness generation
The covenant had nothing to do with Israel
The present generation was included in the covenant
challenge.explanation: Moses emphasizes that the people alive before him that day were participants in the covenant, not only their ancestors.

challenge.question: How do the phrases “face to face” and “I stood between the Lord and you” fit together?
answers: The Lord spoke to the people directly, but Moses mediated in practice
The Lord did not speak to the people at all
Moses replaced the Lord in speaking to the people
challenge.explanation: The people experienced the Lord’s speech directly, but Moses conveyed the words because they feared the fire.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the connection between the people’s fear and their not going up the mountain?
answers: The people wanted to distance themselves from the covenant
Fear kept the people from approaching the mountain
The people had already gone up before Moses
challenge.explanation: The passage connects the people’s fear of the fire with their not going up the mountain.

questions.question: What is emphasized by Moses saying that the covenant was made “with us,” not only with their fathers?
answers: The covenant belonged only to the wilderness generation
The covenant had nothing to do with Israel
The present generation was included in the covenant
questions.explanation: Moses emphasizes that the people alive before him that day were participants in the covenant, not only their ancestors.

questions.question: How do the phrases “face to face” and “I stood between the Lord and you” fit together?
answers: The Lord spoke to the people directly, but Moses mediated in practice
The Lord did not speak to the people at all
Moses replaced the Lord in speaking to the people
questions.explanation: The people experienced the Lord’s speech directly, but Moses conveyed the words because they feared the fire.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the connection between the people’s fear and their not going up the mountain?
answers: The people wanted to distance themselves from the covenant
Fear kept the people from approaching the mountain
The people had already gone up before Moses
questions.explanation: The passage connects the people’s fear of the fire with their not going up the mountain.

paragraphs.title: The Lord Frees Israel from Slavery and Warns Against Idolatry

easy.question: Who says, “I am the Lord thy God”?
answers: The Lord
Moses
Pharaoh
easy.explanation: The speaker identifies himself as the Lord, Israel’s God.

easy.question: From where did the Lord bring the Israelites out?
answers: The land of Canaan
The land of Egypt
The wilderness of Sinai
easy.explanation: The verse says that the Lord brought them out of Egypt, the house of bondage.

easy.question: What are the people forbidden to do?
answers: Build houses
Travel in the wilderness
Make and worship an image
easy.explanation: The verses forbid making images and bowing down to or serving them.

medium.question: What is the correct order of ideas in these verses?
answers: The Lord rescues Israel from Egypt, forbids other gods, and forbids images
Images are forbidden, then the exodus occurs, then other gods are worshiped
Other gods are worshiped, images are forbidden, and then the exodus occurs
medium.explanation: The Lord first recalls the exodus, then forbids other gods, and finally explains the prohibition against images.

medium.question: In the phrase “visiting the iniquity of the fathers,” what does “visiting” mean?
answers: Forgetting
Taking the iniquity into account and bringing consequences
Praising
medium.explanation: Here, “visiting” means taking the iniquity into account and bringing consequences or punishment.

medium.question: Why is the Lord called a “jealous God” after the prohibition against images?
answers: To describe his power in war
To explain why Israel should build images
To emphasize that he requires exclusive loyalty
medium.explanation: The title emphasizes that the Lord requires exclusive loyalty and will not accept worship of other gods.

challenge.question: What is the main difference between “Thou shalt have none other gods before me” and “Thou shalt not make thee any graven image”?
answers: The first forbids loyalty to other gods, while the second forbids making idols
The first concerns only Egypt, while the second concerns only the wilderness
There is no difference
challenge.explanation: The first command concerns whom one worships, while the second concerns making an image for idolatrous worship.

challenge.question: What striking numerical contrast appears between punishment and mercy?
answers: Punishment lasts for thousands, while mercy lasts for one generation
Iniquity is mentioned to the third and fourth generation, while mercy is shown to thousands
Both punishment and mercy last only one generation
challenge.explanation: The passage mentions the third and fourth generation for iniquity but thousands for mercy, emphasizing the abundance of mercy.

challenge.question: Why does the Lord mention the exodus before forbidding other gods and images?
answers: To teach that Egypt is above the heavens
To explain how images were made
To establish his authority and Israel’s obligation to be loyal to him as their deliverer
challenge.explanation: Mentioning the rescue from slavery presents the Lord as Israel’s deliverer and grounds his demand for loyalty.

questions.question: What is the main difference between “Thou shalt have none other gods before me” and “Thou shalt not make thee any graven image”?
answers: The first forbids loyalty to other gods, while the second forbids making idols
The first concerns only Egypt, while the second concerns only the wilderness
There is no difference
questions.explanation: The first command concerns whom one worships, while the second concerns making an image for idolatrous worship.

questions.question: What striking numerical contrast appears between punishment and mercy?
answers: Punishment lasts for thousands, while mercy lasts for one generation
Iniquity is mentioned to the third and fourth generation, while mercy is shown to thousands
Both punishment and mercy last only one generation
questions.explanation: The passage mentions the third and fourth generation for iniquity but thousands for mercy, emphasizing the abundance of mercy.

questions.question: Why does the Lord mention the exodus before forbidding other gods and images?
answers: To teach that Egypt is above the heavens
To explain how images were made
To establish his authority and Israel’s obligation to be loyal to him as their deliverer
questions.explanation: Mentioning the rescue from slavery presents the Lord as Israel’s deliverer and grounds his demand for loyalty.

easy.question: What is forbidden in this verse?
answers: Taking the Lord’s name in vain
Building a house
Leaving the land of Israel
easy.explanation: The verse commands the people not to take the Lord’s name in vain.

easy.question: What does the verse say about the Lord toward anyone who takes his name in vain?
answers: He will bless him
He will not hold him guiltless
He will praise him
easy.explanation: The verse says that the Lord will not hold such a person guiltless.

easy.question: Whose name must not be taken in vain?
answers: Moses’ name
The king’s name
The name of the Lord thy God
easy.explanation: The command specifically concerns the name of the Lord thy God.

medium.question: What is the connection between the command and the words “the Lord will not hold him guiltless”?
answers: They explain that violating the command has serious consequences
They cancel the command
They identify a location
medium.explanation: The words connect the prohibition with a warning about its serious consequences.

medium.question: In the phrase “take the name of the Lord thy God in vain,” what does “in vain” mean?
answers: Joyfully
Meaninglessly, falsely, or without proper justification
Secretly
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to using the Lord’s name emptily, falsely, or improperly.

medium.question: What is the order of ideas in the verse?
answers: The Lord punishes, and then the person takes his name in vain
The person receives a blessing, and then swears an oath
The person takes the Lord’s name in vain, and then the warning is given
medium.explanation: The prohibition comes first, followed by the warning about its consequence.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “in vain”?
answers: The command does not necessarily forbid every mention of the Lord’s name, but forbids empty or improper use
The Lord’s name may never be mentioned
The Lord’s name may be used in any situation
challenge.explanation: “In vain” limits the prohibition to empty, false, or improper use of the Lord’s name.

challenge.question: What function does the word “for” serve in “for the Lord will not hold him guiltless”?
answers: It introduces a question
It gives the reason or explanation for the warning
It identifies a time
challenge.explanation: “For” explains why the command must be taken seriously: the Lord will not hold the offender guiltless.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “take the name ... in vain” emphasize about the command?
answers: It concerns a journey through the wilderness
It teaches that the name belongs to Moses
It links taking the name with using it improperly or emptily
challenge.explanation: The wording connects taking the Lord’s name with using it in a false, empty, or improper way.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “in vain”?
answers: The command does not necessarily forbid every mention of the Lord’s name, but forbids empty or improper use
The Lord’s name may never be mentioned
The Lord’s name may be used in any situation
questions.explanation: “In vain” limits the prohibition to empty, false, or improper use of the Lord’s name.

questions.question: What function does the word “for” serve in “for the Lord will not hold him guiltless”?
answers: It introduces a question
It gives the reason or explanation for the warning
It identifies a time
questions.explanation: “For” explains why the command must be taken seriously: the Lord will not hold the offender guiltless.

questions.question: What does the phrase “take the name ... in vain” emphasize about the command?
answers: It concerns a journey through the wilderness
It teaches that the name belongs to Moses
It links taking the name with using it improperly or emptily
questions.explanation: The wording connects taking the Lord’s name with using it in a false, empty, or improper way.

paragraphs.title: The Sabbath as a Day of Rest for All

easy.question: Which day are the people commanded to keep and sanctify?
answers: The Sabbath day
The first day
Every Friday
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Keep the sabbath day to sanctify it.”

easy.question: How many days are appointed for work?
answers: Five days
Six days
Seven days
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Six days thou shalt labour.”

easy.question: Who must not do any work on the seventh day?
answers: Only the head of the household
Only the servants
The people, their families, servants, animals, and strangers
easy.explanation: The verse lists sons, daughters, servants, animals, and the stranger within the gates.

medium.question: Why must Israel remember that they were servants in Egypt?
answers: So they could work on the Sabbath
Because the Lord brought them out, and therefore commanded them to keep the Sabbath
To remember the names of Egypt’s kings
medium.explanation: The passage connects the exodus with the command to keep the Sabbath.

medium.question: What is the purpose expressed by “that thy manservant and thy maidservant may rest as well as thou”?
answers: Before they work
So that they may rest
Even though they work
medium.explanation: The Sabbath command is intended to give servants rest as well as their masters.

medium.question: What order of events is described?
answers: Six days of work, followed by rest on the seventh
One day of work and six days of rest
Rest first, followed by work without stopping
medium.explanation: The passage first names six working days and then the seventh as a day of Sabbath rest.

challenge.question: What social principle can be inferred from servants resting “as well as thou”?
answers: Only household heads deserve rest
Sabbath rest is intended for everyone in the household, not only the master
Servants must work on the seventh day
challenge.explanation: The phrase places servants’ rest on the same level as the commanded person’s rest, recalling Israel’s slavery in Egypt.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the mention of the ox, ass, and cattle in the Sabbath command?
answers: Working animals must also stop working
Only animals may work on the Sabbath
Animals are unrelated to the command
challenge.explanation: The command includes animals, showing that Sabbath rest is not limited to human beings.

challenge.question: Which combination best describes the Sabbath command?
answers: Remembering the Sabbath, sanctifying it, and refraining from work
Working on the Sabbath and remembering it in the evening
Sanctifying Friday only and avoiding work that day
challenge.explanation: The passage includes sanctifying the Sabbath and refraining from work on the seventh day.

questions.question: What social principle can be inferred from servants resting “as well as thou”?
answers: Only household heads deserve rest
Sabbath rest is intended for everyone in the household, not only the master
Servants must work on the seventh day
questions.explanation: The phrase places servants’ rest on the same level as the commanded person’s rest, recalling Israel’s slavery in Egypt.

questions.question: What can be understood from the mention of the ox, ass, and cattle in the Sabbath command?
answers: Working animals must also stop working
Only animals may work on the Sabbath
Animals are unrelated to the command
questions.explanation: The command includes animals, showing that Sabbath rest is not limited to human beings.

questions.question: Which combination best describes the Sabbath command?
answers: Remembering the Sabbath, sanctifying it, and refraining from work
Working on the Sabbath and remembering it in the evening
Sanctifying Friday only and avoiding work that day
questions.explanation: The passage includes sanctifying the Sabbath and refraining from work on the seventh day.

easy.question: Whom does the verse command people to honor?
answers: Their father and mother
The king of Israel
Their neighbors
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Honour thy father and thy mother.”

easy.question: Who commanded the honoring of parents?
answers: The parents alone
The Lord thy God
The elders of the people
easy.explanation: The verse says, “as the Lord thy God hath commanded thee.”

easy.question: What does the verse promise those who honor their parents?
answers: Wealth and honor
Victory in war
Long life and well-being
easy.explanation: The verse promises prolonged days and that it will go well with them.

medium.question: What connection does the verse make between honoring parents and a person’s future?
answers: Honoring parents is connected with long life and well-being
Honoring parents causes a person to leave the land
Honoring parents removes every other command
medium.explanation: The verse connects honoring parents with prolonged days and well-being.

medium.question: What does “as the Lord thy God hath commanded thee” mean?
answers: As the parents requested
As the Lord commanded and taught
As people do in the land
medium.explanation: The phrase makes clear that honoring parents is a command from the Lord.

medium.question: What purpose is expressed by “that thy days may be prolonged”?
answers: Before a person leaves
Even though a person leaves
So that the person’s days may be prolonged
medium.explanation: The phrase describes the result associated with honoring one’s parents.

challenge.question: How many distinct results of honoring parents does the verse mention?
answers: Two: long life and well-being
One: receiving the land
Three: wealth, health, and honor
challenge.explanation: The verse mentions prolonged days and that it will go well with the person.

challenge.question: What does “in the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee” teach?
answers: Parents give the land to their children
The land is presented as a gift from the Lord
The person no longer lives in the land
challenge.explanation: The wording presents the land as something the Lord gives to Israel.

challenge.question: To whom does “that it may go well with thee” refer?
answers: The father and mother
The land
The person commanded to honor the parents
challenge.explanation: “With thee” refers to the person receiving the command.

questions.question: How many distinct results of honoring parents does the verse mention?
answers: Two: long life and well-being
One: receiving the land
Three: wealth, health, and honor
questions.explanation: The verse mentions prolonged days and that it will go well with the person.

questions.question: What does “in the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee” teach?
answers: Parents give the land to their children
The land is presented as a gift from the Lord
The person no longer lives in the land
questions.explanation: The wording presents the land as something the Lord gives to Israel.

questions.question: To whom does “that it may go well with thee” refer?
answers: The father and mother
The land
The person commanded to honor the parents
questions.explanation: “With thee” refers to the person receiving the command.

paragraphs.title: Prohibitions Against Harming People and Their Possessions

easy.question: What is forbidden in the first command?
answers: Killing
Lying to yourself
Dreaming
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Thou shalt not kill.”

easy.question: Against whom must one not bear false witness?
answers: The king
Your neighbor
The enemy
easy.explanation: The verse forbids bearing false witness against one’s neighbor.

easy.question: What must one not desire or covet?
answers: Only a house
Only a field
Anything belonging to one’s neighbor
easy.explanation: The verse lists the neighbor’s house, field, servants, animals, and everything else belonging to him.

medium.question: What idea is shared by the prohibition against desiring a neighbor’s wife and coveting his possessions?
answers: One must not want for oneself what belongs to another
One must not work in a field
One must not speak with one’s neighbor
medium.explanation: Both prohibitions concern wanting something that belongs to another person.

medium.question: What does “false witness” mean?
answers: Important testimony
Dishonest testimony
Lengthy testimony
medium.explanation: False witness means testimony that is untrue.

medium.question: What is the order of the prohibitions in these verses?
answers: Coveting, stealing, killing, and testimony
Testimony, coveting, killing, and adultery
Killing, adultery, stealing, false witness, and coveting
medium.explanation: The passage lists killing, adultery, stealing, and false witness, followed by prohibitions against desire and coveting.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from separating “Thou shalt not desire thy neighbour’s wife” from “Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s house”?
answers: The prohibition includes both the neighbor’s wife and possessions, but lists them separately
Only objects may be coveted
Only people may be coveted
challenge.explanation: The passage names the neighbor’s wife separately from his house and possessions to show the breadth of the prohibition.

challenge.question: What is the main change in the sequence of commands from verse 17 to verse 18?
answers: It moves from possessions to speech only
It moves from outward acts and words to inward desires
It moves from commands about people to commands about animals only
challenge.explanation: The earlier commands concern acts and speech, while the final command reaches into a person’s inner desires.

challenge.question: What detail emphasizes that the prohibition covers many kinds of property?
answers: The repetition of “thou shalt not”
The mention of “thy neighbour” alone
The list of a house, field, servants, animals, and everything belonging to the neighbor
challenge.explanation: The detailed list, ending with “anything that is thy neighbour’s,” broadens the prohibition.

questions.question: What can be inferred from separating “Thou shalt not desire thy neighbour’s wife” from “Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s house”?
answers: The prohibition includes both the neighbor’s wife and possessions, but lists them separately
Only objects may be coveted
Only people may be coveted
questions.explanation: The passage names the neighbor’s wife separately from his house and possessions to show the breadth of the prohibition.

questions.question: What is the main change in the sequence of commands from verse 17 to verse 18?
answers: It moves from possessions to speech only
It moves from outward acts and words to inward desires
It moves from commands about people to commands about animals only
questions.explanation: The earlier commands concern acts and speech, while the final command reaches into a person’s inner desires.

questions.question: What detail emphasizes that the prohibition covers many kinds of property?
answers: The repetition of “thou shalt not”
The mention of “thy neighbour” alone
The list of a house, field, servants, animals, and everything belonging to the neighbor
questions.explanation: The detailed list, ending with “anything that is thy neighbour’s,” broadens the prohibition.

paragraphs.title: The Ten Words Are Written on Tablets and the People Are Afraid

easy.question: Who spoke to the entire assembly of Israel on the mountain?
answers: The Lord
Moses
The elders
easy.explanation: The passage says that the Lord spoke to the entire assembly on the mountain.

easy.question: Where did the Lord speak to the people?
answers: At the tent of meeting
On the mountain
In the wilderness
easy.explanation: The passage says that the words were spoken to the people on the mountain.

easy.question: What did the Lord write the words on?
answers: A scroll
A wooden tablet
Two tables of stone
easy.explanation: The Lord wrote the words on two tables of stone.

medium.question: What did the heads of the tribes and the elders do after hearing the voice and seeing the burning mountain?
answers: They came near Moses
They left the camp
They went up the mountain alone
medium.explanation: After hearing and seeing this scene, the leaders came near Moses.

medium.question: What does “thick darkness” describe in this passage?
answers: Bright light
Heavy darkness or gloom
A loud noise
medium.explanation: The phrase describes a dark, clouded atmosphere surrounding the fire.

medium.question: Why did the people ask Moses to hear the Lord’s words for them?
answers: They did not want to leave the camp
Moses had already received the tablets
They feared that the fire or the voice would kill them
medium.explanation: The people said that if they continued hearing the Lord’s voice from the fire, they might die.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the people’s request that Moses mediate between them and the Lord?
answers: They believed another direct encounter with the voice and fire was dangerous
They thought Moses could not hear the Lord
They wanted to prevent Moses from receiving the tablets
challenge.explanation: The people recognized the greatness of the event but feared that further direct contact with the voice and fire would kill them.

challenge.question: What does the people’s promise, “we will hear it, and do it,” mean?
answers: They would listen but not act
They would listen to the Lord and obey his words
They would ask Moses only to explain the words
challenge.explanation: The people promise not only to hear the Lord’s words but also to do them.

challenge.question: What distinguishes the Lord’s action from Moses’ action in the passage?
answers: Moses spoke from the fire and the Lord approached the people
The people wrote the words and Moses heard them
The Lord wrote the words on the tablets and delivered them to Moses
challenge.explanation: The passage says that the Lord wrote the words on the stone tablets and delivered them to Moses.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the people’s request that Moses mediate between them and the Lord?
answers: They believed another direct encounter with the voice and fire was dangerous
They thought Moses could not hear the Lord
They wanted to prevent Moses from receiving the tablets
questions.explanation: The people recognized the greatness of the event but feared that further direct contact with the voice and fire would kill them.

questions.question: What does the people’s promise, “we will hear it, and do it,” mean?
answers: They would listen but not act
They would listen to the Lord and obey his words
They would ask Moses only to explain the words
questions.explanation: The people promise not only to hear the Lord’s words but also to do them.

questions.question: What distinguishes the Lord’s action from Moses’ action in the passage?
answers: Moses spoke from the fire and the Lord approached the people
The people wrote the words and Moses heard them
The Lord wrote the words on the tablets and delivered them to Moses
questions.explanation: The passage says that the Lord wrote the words on the stone tablets and delivered them to Moses.

paragraphs.title: The Lord Approves the People’s Request

easy.question: Who heard the voice of the people’s words?
answers: The Lord
Moses
The people
easy.explanation: The verse says, “The Lord heard the voice of your words.”

easy.question: To whom did the people speak before the Lord spoke to Moses?
answers: Aaron
Moses
Their children
easy.explanation: The Lord says that the people spoke to Moses.

easy.question: What did the Lord want the people to do always?
answers: Build cities
Go to war
Fear the Lord and keep his commandments
easy.explanation: The Lord wanted their hearts to fear him and for them to keep all his commandments.

medium.question: What order of events is described?
answers: The Lord gave commands, then the people spoke, and finally Moses heard
The people spoke to Moses, the Lord heard, and then the Lord responded to Moses
Moses spoke to the people, the people listened, and then the Lord answered
medium.explanation: The people first spoke to Moses, the Lord heard them, and then he told Moses his response.

medium.question: What does “that it might be well with them and with their children” mean?
answers: They would be punished
They would be separated
Things would go well for them
medium.explanation: The phrase promises well-being for the people and their children if they fear the Lord and keep his commandments.

medium.question: Why should the people fear the Lord and keep his commandments?
answers: So that it might be well with them and their children forever
So that they could speak in Moses’ place
So that the Lord would hear only their voices
medium.explanation: The verse explicitly gives their long-term well-being as the purpose.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the Lord’s statement, “They have well said all that they have spoken”?
answers: The people had already kept every commandment
The people said nothing
The Lord approved what the people had said
challenge.explanation: The Lord approved their words but immediately expressed the hope that they would continue to fear him and keep his commandments.

challenge.question: What does “such an heart in them” emphasize?
answers: That fear of the Lord should be an inner and lasting quality
That the people must change where they live
That the statement refers only to the voice the Lord heard
challenge.explanation: “Heart” points to the people’s inner character and desire; the Lord wants their good response to become permanent.

challenge.question: What does “with them, and with their children for ever” teach about obedience?
answers: Its benefit lasts only during Moses’ lifetime
Its benefit extends to future generations and lasts over time
The commandments are intended only for children
challenge.explanation: The phrase extends the benefit from the people to their children and emphasizes its lasting character.

questions.question: What can be understood from the Lord’s statement, “They have well said all that they have spoken”?
answers: The people had already kept every commandment
The people said nothing
The Lord approved what the people had said
questions.explanation: The Lord approved their words but immediately expressed the hope that they would continue to fear him and keep his commandments.

questions.question: What does “such an heart in them” emphasize?
answers: That fear of the Lord should be an inner and lasting quality
That the people must change where they live
That the statement refers only to the voice the Lord heard
questions.explanation: “Heart” points to the people’s inner character and desire; the Lord wants their good response to become permanent.

questions.question: What does “with them, and with their children for ever” teach about obedience?
answers: Its benefit lasts only during Moses’ lifetime
Its benefit extends to future generations and lasts over time
The commandments are intended only for children
questions.explanation: The phrase extends the benefit from the people to their children and emphasizes its lasting character.

paragraphs.title: Moses Remains with the Lord and Receives the Law

easy.question: Where were the people told to return?
answers: To their tents
To Egypt
To another mountain
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Get you into your tents again.”

easy.question: Who was commanded to remain there?
answers: All the people
Moses
The elders
easy.explanation: Moses was told, “Stand thou here by me.”

easy.question: What would Moses receive and teach the people?
answers: All the commandments, statutes, and judgments
The names of all the tents
Ways of conducting trade
easy.explanation: The Lord told Moses to receive and teach the people the commandments, statutes, and judgments.

medium.question: Why did Moses remain while the people returned to their tents?
answers: To receive the law from the Lord and teach it to the people
To build new tents
To search for Egypt
medium.explanation: Moses remained to hear the Lord’s commands and judgments and teach them to the people.

medium.question: What does “to possess it” mean in the phrase about the land the Lord gives them?
answers: To leave it
To receive it as an inheritance and occupy it
To hide it
medium.explanation: The context shows that the Lord gives the land to Israel as an inheritance to possess.

medium.question: What order of events is described?
answers: The people return to their tents, and Moses remains to receive instructions
Moses returns to his tent, and the people receive instructions
The people enter the land, and only afterward Moses hears the commandments
medium.explanation: The people are first told to return to their tents, while Moses remains with the Lord to receive instructions.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the command to “do them in the land”?
answers: The commandments were meant only to be heard
The people were expected to practice the commandments in the land they would receive
The commandments were intended only for Moses
challenge.explanation: The command to do them shows that the people were to practice them in the land the Lord would give them.

challenge.question: To whom does “teach them” refer?
answers: Moses, who would teach the people
The tents, which would teach the people
The land, which would teach the people
challenge.explanation: The Lord is speaking to Moses and commands him to teach the people.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “all the commandments, statutes, and judgments” emphasize?
answers: Moses would receive only one law
The people would receive only partial instructions

paragraphs.title: Walking in the Lord’s Way Brings Life and Blessing

easy.question: What did the Lord command the people to do?
answers: Keep and do his commandments
Leave the land
Choose a new king
easy.explanation: The passage commands them to keep and do what the Lord has commanded.

easy.question: From what must the people not turn?
answers: The road through the wilderness
To the right hand or the left from the Lord’s commands
From the land of Israel
easy.explanation: They are told not to turn aside to the right hand or the left.

easy.question: What will happen if they walk in the way the Lord commanded?
answers: They will live, prosper, and have long life in the land
They will return to Egypt
They will no longer need to keep commandments
easy.explanation: The passage promises life, prosperity, and long days in the land.

medium.question: What cause-and-effect relationship appears in these verses?
answers: Keeping the Lord’s commandments leads to life and well-being

Walking right leads to long life
medium.explanation: Walking in the way commanded by the Lord is presented as the cause of life and well-being.

medium.question: What does “possess the land” mean in this context?

Give it to others
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to receiving the land and settling in it.

medium.question: What order of ideas appears in the passage?
answers: Receiving the land, then keeping the commandments, and finally the command
Keeping the Lord’s commandments, walking in his way, and then enjoying life in the land
Leaving the land, following another way, and finally having long life
medium.explanation: The people are first commanded to keep and do the commandments, then to walk in the Lord’s way, resulting in life and prosperity.

A particular way is required only during war
All the Lord’s instructions must be followed rather than selected ones

To distinguish between two lands
To command alternating between right and left
challenge.explanation: The two expressions complement each other: do not depart from the way, and continue walking in it.

Several positive results of walking in the Lord’s way are listed
Life is promised only after leaving the land
